rule.title: Explicit Definition of Bounded Contexts
rule.statement: Each subsystem must maintain an explicit Bounded Context with its own Ubiquitous Language; domain models must not be shared indiscriminately across contexts.
rule.rationale: Sharing a single entity class across ingestion, billing, vector indexing, and chat results in an bloated entity with conflicting invariants.
rule.implementation_guidance: Define separate models for IngestionDocument (file buffer, extraction metadata) and RagDocument (vector embeddings, chunks, citations).

forbidden.example: A single giant Document class with 50 optional properties catering to every subsystem.

preferred.example: Separate DocumentIngestionEntity and RagVectorEntity with explicit boundary mapper.

source.evidence_quote: A bounded context is a boundary within a domain where a particular domain model applies... dividing a system into bounded contexts protects against model pollution.

rule.title: Anti-Corruption Layer (ACL) for External Services
rule.statement: Third-party APIs (e.g. Gemini, DeepSeek, S3) must be isolated behind an Anti-Corruption Layer (ACL) that translates vendor payloads into internal domain models.
rule.rationale: Directly exposing external schemas in application code tightly couples the codebase to third-party vendor contracts, making provider switching or SDK upgrades painful.
rule.implementation_guidance: Wrap external clients in adapter classes (e.g., GeminiEmbeddingAdapter) implementing an internal interface (IEmbeddingService).

forbidden.example: Passing GoogleGenAI.GenerateContentResponse directly through controllers and services.

source.evidence_quote: An anti-corruption layer translates between two bounded contexts or an external system, preventing foreign concepts and models from polluting the internal model.

rule.title: Aggregate Root Invariant Encapsulation and Transactional Boundary
rule.statement: Domain mutations must be executed strictly through the Aggregate Root entity; external code must never directly alter the state of child entities within an aggregate boundary.
rule.rationale: Bypassing the Aggregate Root to modify child records directly corrupts domain invariants and breaks consistency guarantees within the business model.
rule.implementation_guidance: KnowledgeBase is the Aggregate Root. To add or reorder documents and chunks, invoke kb.addDocument(...) rather than executing direct Prisma mutations on Document or Chunk tables.

forbidden.example: await prisma.chunk.update({ where: { id: chunkId }, data: { status: 'processed' } }); // Bypassing KnowledgeBase invariant

preferred.example: const kb = await kbRepo.findById(kbId); kb.markChunkProcessed(chunkId); await kbRepo.save(kb);

source.section: The Aggregate Pattern and Invariant Protection
source.evidence_quote: An Aggregate is an explicit boundary around a cluster of entities and value objects. All modifications must enter through the Aggregate Root to protect consistency invariants.

rule.title: Domain Events and Transactional Outbox for Asynchronous Decoupling
rule.statement: Cross-subsystem side effects (e.g. triggering embedding, vector indexing, email notifications) must be emitted as Domain Events and committed via the Transactional Outbox pattern within the same database transaction.
rule.rationale: Directly calling external message queues or third-party APIs inside a database transaction leads to dual-write inconsistencies if the network or transaction aborts.
rule.implementation_guidance: Save the business entity and an OutboxEvent row inside a single prisma.$transaction. An independent background worker polls and dispatches outbox events reliably.

forbidden.example: await prisma.document.create({ data }); await rabbitmq.publish('doc_created', data); // Dual-write risk: if MQ fails, state is inconsistent

source.section: The Outbox Pattern for Reliable Messaging
source.evidence_quote: To avoid dual-write inconsistencies when publishing domain events, commit the event to an outbox table within the same database transaction as the entity state.
